```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = TRUE)
input_file <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
active_file <- if (requireNamespace("rstudioapi", quietly = TRUE) && rstudioapi::isAvailable())
  tryCatch(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path, error = function(e) "") else ""
input_dirs <- c(if (length(input_file) == 1L && !is.na(input_file) && nzchar(input_file)) dirname(input_file),
                if (nzchar(active_file)) dirname(active_file), getwd())
candidates <- unique(unlist(lapply(input_dirs, function(p)
  c(p, file.path(p, ".."), file.path(p, "with_intercept")))))
valid <- vapply(candidates, function(p) file.exists(file.path(p, "R", "gfm_baseline.R")), logical(1))
if (!any(valid)) stop("Cannot locate with_intercept/R/gfm_baseline.R; keep the package directories together.")
project_root <- normalizePath(candidates[which(valid)[1L]], mustWork = TRUE)
baseline_root <- file.path(project_root, "R")
source(file.path(baseline_root, "gfm_baseline.R"), local = knitr::knit_global())
if (!isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress")) || !exists("params", inherits = FALSE)) {
  parsed <- knitr::knit_params(readLines(file.path(project_root, "simulations", "all_nodes.Rmd"), warn = FALSE))
  params <- lapply(parsed, function(x) x$value)
}
lambda_values <- if (is.character(params$lambda_values)) {
  as.numeric(trimws(strsplit(params$lambda_values, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]))
} else as.numeric(params$lambda_values)
K <- if (is.null(params$k)) length(lambda_values) else params$k
models <- if (identical(params$model, "all")) c("gaussian", "logit", "poisson", "probit") else params$model
control <- Filter(Negate(is.null), list(
  learning_rate = params$learning_rate, max_iter = params$max_iter,
  tolerance = params$tolerance, M_bound_U = params$M_bound_U,
  M_bound_alpha = params$M_bound_alpha, M_bound_Lambda = params$M_bound_Lambda,
  probability_eps = params$probability_eps,
  max_debias_memory_mb = params$max_debias_memory_mb, backtracking = params$backtracking
))
# NULL selects at most seven workers; 1 selects one.
n_cores <- if (is.null(params$n_cores)) {
  min(7L, max(1L, parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE) - 1L, na.rm = TRUE))
} else as.integer(params$n_cores)
output_dir <- if (is.null(params$output_dir)) file.path(project_root, "data", "baseline",
  paste0("alpha_", params$alpha_normalization)) else params$output_dir
```

This is the all-node entry point for the same centered baseline estimator.
It uses $a_i\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathrm{Uniform}(-2,0)$ and $\alpha_i^\star=a_i/\|a\|_2$ and
$\Theta_{ij}^\star=\alpha_i^\star+\alpha_j^\star+
(u_i^\star)^\top\Lambda^\star u_j^\star$.

`run_simulation` defaults to `false`. The small configuration has 60 nodes
and three independently generated networks per observation model.
The latent truth and node effects stay fixed across repetitions and models.
Global Lambda correction is disabled here by default; set `debias: true`
explicitly to compute it. The default `pdf_bp_bm` correction retains the theory BP formula,
includes BM once, and uses the reviewed exact finite-sample projector
(see `node_inference.Rmd`). Both entry points call
the same core functions.
`n_cores` sets how many worker processes fit the networks in parallel
(`null` uses at most seven physical cores, `1` uses one worker); results
are identical either way.
YAML controls set to `null` keep core defaults; non-null overrides are passed
to `gfb_config()` and saved with the run settings.

Save YAML edits before running setup or Run All. Interactive execution
reloads saved values each time; Knit with Parameters retains supplied overrides.
`worker_backend: "in_process"` and `n_cores: 1` are the portable trial defaults.
For parallel runs explicitly select `worker_backend: "psock"` and a worker count.
This notebook uses the ordinary R implementation for fitting and inference.

The default `alpha_normalization: "l2"` first samples raw
$a_i\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathrm{Uniform}(-2,0)$, then uses
$\alpha_i^\star=a_i/\sqrt{\sum_j a_j^2}$, so $\|\alpha^\star\|_2=1$.
The transformed components share a random denominator: they are dependent,
are no longer Uniform(-2,0), and their typical scale decreases as $n^{-1/2}$.
This changes the data-generating design, not the estimation constraints,
full-matrix initialization, optimizer controls or BP+BM correction.
Set `alpha_normalization: "none"` to reproduce the original unscaled draws.
Saved truth retains `alpha_raw` and normalization metadata. The default output
and figure paths separate `alpha_l2` from `alpha_none`; an explicitly supplied
`output_dir` or `figure_dir` remains in effect. Do not combine different
generation modes or existing screening results in one evaluation.

## Fixed design

```{r truth}
truth <- gfb_generate_truth(
  n = params$n, K = K, lambda_values = lambda_values,
  design_seed = params$design_seed, alpha_seed = params$alpha_seed,
  alpha_min = params$alpha_min, alpha_max = params$alpha_max, alpha_normalization = params$alpha_normalization
)
truth$diagnostics
data.frame(alpha_normalization = params$alpha_normalization,
           alpha_raw_l2_norm = sqrt(sum(truth$alpha_raw^2)),
           alpha_model_l2_norm = sqrt(sum(truth$alpha_star^2)))
data.frame(alpha_min_observed = min(truth$alpha_star),
           alpha_max_observed = max(truth$alpha_star),
           max_center_error = max(abs(colSums(truth$U_star))),
           max_orthogonality_error = max(abs(crossprod(truth$U_star) / params$n - diag(K))))
```

## Fit and infer all nodes

```{r simulate}
simulation <- NULL
if (isTRUE(params$run_simulation)) {
  simulation <- gfb_run_simulation(
    n = params$n, K = K, models = models, n_sim = params$n_sim,
    nodes = seq_len(params$n), lambda_values = lambda_values,
    sigma = params$sigma, design_seed = params$design_seed,
    alpha_seed = params$alpha_seed, replication_seed_base = params$replication_seed_base,
    alpha_min = params$alpha_min, alpha_max = params$alpha_max, alpha_normalization = params$alpha_normalization,
    control = control, debias = params$debias, debias_method = params$debias_method,
    output_dir = output_dir, run_id = params$run_id, save_fits = params$save_fits,
    n_cores = n_cores,
    worker_backend = params$worker_backend,
    inference_workers = params$inference_workers
  )
  print(simulation$fit_summary)
  cat("Saved run:", simulation$run_dir, "\n")
} else {
  cat("Truth checked. No networks were fitted and no simulation files were written.\n")
}
```

```{r node-status}
if (!is.null(simulation)) {
  print(table(simulation$fit_summary$model, simulation$fit_summary$status))
  if (nrow(simulation$node_summary)) {
    print(table(simulation$node_summary$model, simulation$node_summary$status))
    print(utils::head(simulation$node_summary, 12L))
  }
}
```

Rows in `node_summary` are keyed by model, replicate and node. Joint
standardization has $K+1$ coordinates; `alpha_marginal_z` is a separate
univariate node-effect statistic. Failed fits and invalid node information
are retained and explicitly flagged. Nodes from the same network are
dependent; pooled node rows must not be interpreted as independent Monte
Carlo repetitions. Three repetitions verify execution, not calibration.
`fit$diagnostics$one_sided_nodes` identifies binary nodes with all-zero or
all-one incident observations and Poisson nodes with all-zero observations.
Inference is unavailable for those fits even if the numerical residual is tiny.

The results use fresh run directories below `data/baseline/alpha_l2/` by default; original
simulation results are untouched. The plotting notebook reads these saved
results and generates per-node QQ figures without fitting new models.
